targets.summary: Building py_args with py::make_tuple creates a full tuple when it isn't needed; a ternary would avoid the allocation.
targets.adoption_evidence: Before: `py::tuple py_args; if (args == Py_None) { py_args = py::make_tuple(); } else { py_args = py::reinterpret_borrow<py::tuple>(args); }`. Merged: `py::tuple py_args = args == Py_None ? py::make_tuple() : py::reinterpret_borrow<py::tuple>(args);`. The if/else became the ternary the maintainer suggested, so py_args is no longer default-constructed and then reassigned.
targets.stage3_reason: The merged code adopted the suggested ternary (`py::tuple py_args = args == Py_None ? py::make_tuple() : ...`). But avoiding one throwaway empty tuple from the default-constructed `py::tuple py_args;` is a micro-optimization nit, not a defect.
